ROOT CAUSE (Phase 1 — PROVEN) — flaky test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket

## Verdict
The failure is a **test-infrastructure defect** in `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse `_network_guard` fixture, NOT a defect in `test_serve` or in product code. The guard patches `socket.socket.connect` in a way that is **not restore-safe**, and under full-suite `-n 4 --dist worksteal` load it **leaks the guard permanently** onto the worker process, so every later `@pytest.mark.allow_network` test on that worker — `test_serve` among them — is wrongly blocked with `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests`.

## The leaked state — decisive CI evidence
From the three failing CI runs (33333653370 / 33332386485 / 33331343082, all on `popen-gw1`, both py3.12 and py3.13), the test_serve traceback bottom is:

    http/client.py:1051  connect -> self.sock = self._create_connection(...)
    socket.py:850 (3.12) / 853 (3.13):  in create_connection      <-- REAL body reached
        sock.connect(sa)
    conftest.py  _guard_socket_connect:  raise RuntimeError(
        "Network access is forbidden ... Mock the network call
         (e.g. unittest.mock.patch('urllib.request.urlopen')) ...")

Two facts are decisive:
1. Execution **entered the real `socket.create_connection` body** (reached socket.py:850 and its `sock.connect(sa)` line) — so `socket.create_connection` was **NOT patched** (real).
2. `sock.connect(sa)` hit `_guard_socket_connect` and raised the **connect-guard** message (the one that names `urllib.request.urlopen`), distinct from the create_connection patch's message ("... or add @pytest.mark.allow_network.") — so `socket.socket.connect` **WAS the guard**.

So the process was in the asymmetric state **connect = GUARD, create_connection = real**. This is impossible from `test_serve`'s own fixture (it is `allow_network`, so its guard SKIPS and installs neither patch; and if it did install, it would install BOTH). It is a **leaked, partial guard** left behind by an earlier guarded test.

## Why connect leaks but create_connection does not — mechanism (runtime-proven)
`_network_guard` (committed form) does:

    with (
        patch.object(socket.socket, "connect", _guard_socket_connect),
        patch("socket.create_connection", side_effect=RuntimeError(...)),
    ):
        yield

Key CPython fact (verified at runtime): `socket.socket` is the pure-Python subclass of `_socket.socket`, and it does **not** define its own `connect` — `connect` is **inherited** and is NOT in `socket.socket.__dict__`. `unittest.mock`'s `_patch.get_original()` therefore records `is_local=False` for the FIRST patch and restores by **`delattr`** (removing the override to re-expose the inherited real). But a **second** `patch.object(socket.socket, "connect")` applied while the first is still active sees `connect` already **in** `__dict__`, records `is_local=True` with `temp_original = <the guard>`, and on exit **`setattr`s the guard back permanently**. `socket.create_connection` is a stable **module global** (always in `socket.__dict__`), so its `temp_original` is always the real function and it **cannot** leak this way — which is exactly why CI shows connect leaked but create_connection real.

Runtime proof against the REAL fixture (driving `_network_guard._fixture_function` for two guarded windows with an out-of-LIFO teardown):

    after X enter:            connect=GUARD (in __dict__)
    after Y enter (overlap):  connect=GUARD (Y captured local=True, temp=guard)
    after X teardown (o-o-o): connect=real  (X delattr'd)
    after Y teardown:         connect=GUARD  <-- LEAKED, create_connection=real
    VICTIM allow_network test BLOCKED: RuntimeError "... Mock the network call
      (e.g. unittest.mock.patch('urllib.request.urlopen')) ..."   == the CI failure

I also proved the **self-perpetuation**: once `connect` is stuck in `socket.socket.__dict__` as the guard, EVERY subsequent guarded `_network_guard` window captures `is_local=True, temp_original=<guard>` and **re-installs the guard on its own exit**. So a single seeding event makes the block last for the **entire remaining life of the worker process** — which is why once it trips on `popen-gw1` it reliably fails `test_serve`.

## The seed (what first leaves the connect override installed)
The persistent block only needs to be seeded ONCE: a single guarded `_network_guard` window whose connect override is left installed while `create_connection` is cleanly restored/never-mocked (connect=GUARD, create_connection=real). Within `with (A=connect, B=create_connection)` that is the state either (i) during setup after `A.__enter__` and before `B.__enter__`, or (ii) during teardown after `B.__exit__` and before `A.__exit__` — i.e. a finalization that does not complete `A.__exit__` (an abandoned / out-of-order / interrupted fixture-generator finalization under xdist worksteal load). NOTE: two fully overlapping windows would leak create_connection too, which CI does NOT show; the CI state is specifically a connect-only half-restore. This class of finalization anomaly is what full-suite parallel load perturbs, matching the ticket's "only under full-suite `-n 4 --dist worksteal`" signature.

## Reproduction / failure-rate (accounts for non-determinism)
- Deterministic mechanism reproduction: 100% — the leak and the victim block reproduce every run against the real fixture.
- Full-suite in-situ reproduction of the *seed* on this 18-core box: rare. Across 3 full `pytest -m "not integration and not external and not repo_policy" -n 4 --dist worksteal` runs under moderate bounded CPU load, `test_serve` itself has NOT re-failed (0/3; the seed rate on this hardware is lower than the reporter's 2/2), consistent with a load/timing-sensitive finalization race. A focused high-worker (-n 8) stress loop over the thread-spawning guarded tests + the victim is running to try to trip the seed with instrumentation (owners stack + `conn` state + ANOMALY markers on every PATCH_ENTER/EXIT/SKIP).

## Defect origin (caused_by)
The leak-prone guard entered rebar **verbatim** in the floor extraction commit **b534f47a7f9bf216498bac941a28e9b91c3c3189** ("Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler into standalone rebar", 2026-06-08) — the fixture was imported from digital-service-orchestra as `_dso_network_guard` with the same `patch.object(socket.socket, "connect", _guard_socket_connect)` on the inherited class attribute. So `socket.socket.connect` has been patched leak-unsafely since rebar's first commit; e9d5-c850-d505-4a5a is where the flake was DISCOVERED, not the cause.

## Sibling failures under the same load (Step-7 sweep) — DIFFERENT class
The other tests the ticket lists as failing under the same full-suite load (test_atomic_completion_close.py [x5], test_rebar_repo_isolation.py, test_tracker_footprint_cli.py) reproduce readily under bounded CPU load in my runs while test_serve does not, and they share **no** code path with the socket guard — they are git/filesystem resource-contention flakes, a **separate class**, out of scope for this ticket's fix. (test_check_shellcheck::test_repository_tree_is_currently_clean also failed in my runs, but only because my worktree carries uncommitted debug instrumentation + scripts — an artifact of the investigation, not a real flake.)

## Fix direction (Phase 2)
Make `_network_guard` restore-safe for the inherited `socket.socket.connect` attribute so it can never leak/self-perpetuate: install the override and restore by **unconditional `delattr`** of our own override in a `finally` (idempotent; re-exposes the inherited real; never re-installs a captured `temp_original`), plus have the `allow_network` branch clear any leaked override before yielding so the victim contract holds even against a fresh, not-yet-cleared leak. This eliminates the self-perpetuation that makes the block worker-wide. Test-only change (tests/conftest.py); restores the intended `allow_network` contract without altering product behavior. RED->GREEN with a held-out oracle asserting the invariant "a guarded window's teardown always leaves socket.socket.connect restored, even under overlapping/out-of-order teardown, and an allow_network test is never blocked by a leaked guard."
